comment: The REDDHI framework does not adequately address offline-first data synchronization requirements. In low-connectivity field environments across Sub-Saharan Africa, data collection cannot depend on live connectivity. CHW-facing applications must be able to capture and store data locally and sync reliably to national registries when connectivity is restored. This failure mode is one of the most common causes of data loss and integrity issues in real deployments.

public.text: The REDDHI framework does not adequately address offline-first data synchronization requirements. In low-connectivity field environments across Sub-Saharan Africa, data collection cannot depend on live connectivity. CHW-facing applications must be able to capture and store data locally and sync reliably to national registries when connectivity is restored. This failure mode is one of the most common causes of data loss and integrity issues in real deployments.
public.suggestedRevision: Add a dedicated subsection within REDDHI on offline-first architecture requirements, specifying minimum offline capability standards for field-facing applications and describing acceptable synchronization approaches for low-bandwidth environments.
